The page shows each as one word; ISO 32000-1, 9.4.4 moves the pen by the width of every glyph shown.

overrides.reason: PDF.js reads two words joined across a space glyph the page sets between them, in a line it reorders from right to left. The page shows the gap; ISO 32000-1, 14.8.2.5 makes a space character a word break.

The font draws Kannada glyphs for codes its ToUnicode CMap maps to General Punctuation, so the values ISO 32000-1, 9.10.2 gives are not the page's text in either reading. The two readings differ by the U+200C the CMap gives one painted glyph, which PDF.js drops and litho keeps.

Their baseline segments, turned -26.6 degrees, reach 41.81, 1.43 and 2.56, inside the crop box from 0, and poppler draws all three at 300 dpi. The crop box clips the page's contents, ISO 32000-1, 14.11.2.

PDF.js adds a glyph's advance to its origin in text space, here Tf 1 with the size in Tm (23) and the CTM (1.364): the "É" at x = 403.69 reaches 404.19 and is dropped against the crop box's left edge at 404.22. Its advance in user space runs to 419.28, across the whole crop box, which frames the glyph: poppler at 300 dpi draws the É and nothing else. The crop box clips the page's contents, ISO 32000-1, 14.11.2.

PDF.js tests text turned a quarter by its origin alone. The "J" of each "Job:" is set turned (Tm [0 8 -8 0 743.47 -0.13], Tf 1), its origin 0.13 units under the crop box's bottom edge at 0, its advance running up to 3.87. poppler at 300 dpi draws "Job:" whole.
